caption: The drawing depicts a pair of rectangular, vertically-oriented wooden shutters mounted side by side, each fitted with two metal hinges on the outer edges. The wood is weathered, with visible peeling paint in shades of light gray, off-white, and exposed brown, revealing an uneven, distressed surface. Each shutter features two recessed, diamond-shaped panels bordered by raised molding; the upper and lower panels are identical in shape and size. The hinges are depicted in a rusty brown color, with visible screws attaching them to the wood. There is a small, round metal knob or latch on the right shutter, positioned approximately midway down the edge. The background is a plain, light beige with no other elements, and the artist's name, "Rose Campbell Gerke," is written in small letters near the bottom right of the image.
title: Wooden Cabinet Doors
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
